newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's KJS cautious on coffee retail prices.
newsitem.headline: Germany's KJS cautious on coffee retail prices.

text.p: German coffee market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) said it would tread cautiously before making further retail price hikes although dramatically higher coffee prices would justify them.
"We would be willing and ready to raise retail prices once again but the competition also has to act and so far that has not been convincing," said spokesman Rolf Sauerbier in reponse to an inquiry.
He said further decision-making would be guided by competitors' moves because KJS did not wish to move too far away from the market average.
At this stage, KJS could not set a date for a possible increase, nor indicate its size.
Spectacular rallies on Thursday brought fresh 20-year highs in New York arabicas.
KJS, part of Philip Morris Cos Inc, had planned to raise prices by one mark in early June, following combined price rises by 2.50 marks per 500 grams packet in 1997.
Sauerbier said average KJS prices were at around 8.20 marks on supermarket shelves where coffee industry association DKV said the average market price was 7.90 marks in mid-May.
Sauerbier said announcements by competitor Tchibo, which earlier Friday said further rises were inevitable if the situation stayed as it was, should be viewed with caution.
Tchibo's official price range stood at 8.99-10.99 marks but many of the company's tied shops were undercutting this range with special offers.
A spokesman for German coffee industry association DKV said the fundamentally tight markets could still push higher with the Brazilian winter approaching.
Fear of possible crop damage in Brazil was as supportive as fund interest.
"It's no wonder there are no green coffee buyers at these levels," he said.
But he warned that fund interest could as easily falter as it had emerged.
